summary: Verified Change Password feature end-to-end. Backend: 5/5 pytest cases pass on POST /api/auth/change-password (wrong current -> 400 'Password attuale errata'; short new_password -> 422; same-as-current -> 400 with 'diversa'; missing auth -> 401; success -> 200 {ok:true}, old password no longer logs in, new password logs in, admin password restored to Admin2026!). Frontend: Profile tab shows '🔐 Sicurezza' card with outlined 'Cambia password' button (testID go-change-password) after admin login; tapping navigates to /change-password screen; header 'Cambia password' renders; all three password TextInputs and submit button are visible via their testIDs (current-password, new-password, confirm-password, submit-cp). Client-side mismatch validation ('Le due password non coincidono') and backend error ('Password attuale errata') both surface correctly in the UI. Admin password confirmed restored to Admin2026! after all tests.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~1600+ lines; consider splitting into routers (auth, articles, media, admin, billing) for maintainability.

Change-password endpoint correctly hashes with bcrypt and does not invalidate existing JWTs. Optional hardening: rotate JWT (bump user's token_version) on password change so previously issued tokens stop working.
seed_data_creation: None. No users/articles/media modified. Admin password was temporarily changed inside the success test and then restored to Admin2026! (verified via login 200).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_change_password.py. The pytest.ini uses xdist parallelism; if adding tests that mutate the admin password, either mark them to run in the same worker (module scope) or serialize by using a dedicated non-admin user, otherwise cross-worker races will cause spurious 'Password attuale errata' failures on other change-password tests. Frontend uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (not EXPO_BACKEND_URL).
rca_of_issue: N/A — feature works as designed. The original user-reported symptom (Sicurezza card missing) was purely a stale web preview / Metro cache issue; the code in profile.tsx correctly renders the card and after refresh the button is visible for the admin user.
